title: Some missing tourists make contact as Nepal flood death toll tops 1,100 - WKMG
description: Some missing tourists make contact as Nepal flood death toll tops 1,100  WKMG
publisher.title: WKMG
full_article:
KATHMANDU – Some tourists previously reported missing in Nepal have made contact with authorities, officials said Wednesday, as search efforts continued following catastrophic floods that killed at least 1,118 people and left more than 3,900 missing.

Nepal’s Foreign Ministry said 324 foreign nationals had been rescued so far, while about 590 from 39 countries remained missing a week after the Aug. 26 floods.

Recommended Videos

Missing tourists make contact

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Wednesday that the number of Australians missing in the disaster had fallen from 43 to 38 after five were confirmed safe overnight.

“Amidst all of this tragedy, we are seeing some positive news. Today, another five Australians have been confirmed safe,” Albanese told reporters in Palau, where he is attending a regional summit.

“We hope, of course, for positive news further, and we’re doing everything we can to work with authorities,” Albanese added.

Sunil Sharma, a spokesperson for the Nepal Tourism Board, said at least five other foreign tourists who were previously reported missing had contacted authorities by email or telephone in recent days.

China builds access road for rescue crews

On the Chinese side, rescue crews completed a makeshift road to the disaster site at Gyirong Port on the Nepal border, state broadcaster CCTV reported Wednesday.

Crews have been clearing access for heavy machinery to be used in the search at the border crossing complex, which was washed away by the floods. The road leading to the crossing was destroyed and buried under water, mud and rocks.

China separately reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing as of Sunday.

The disaster began Aug. 26 in the Himalayas, when a glacial collapse sent rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods downstream. The surge entered rivers flowing through Tibet and Nepal, causing them to rise rapidly. Floodwaters swept away homes, buildings, roads and bridges, carrying mud and rocks downstream.

Some survivors find shelter in Kathmandu

Some flood survivors are fleeing the devastation to seek shelter in Nepal's capital Kathmandu.

Around 400 survivors, mostly from the town of Timure about 110 kilometers (65 miles) west of Kathmandu, have been staying at the Yellow Gumba monastery, grieving lost family members and homes while relying on one another for support. The shelter is being organized by locals and relatives, with relief supplies coming from individuals and charity organizations.

Among those at the monastery is 21-year-old Riya Tamang, who fled with her 10-month-old baby as floodwaters approached.

“I was the last one to leave the house. It was so difficult to escape,” she said.

Tamang lost her grandparents in the disaster. Her husband, who works as a cook in Gyirong town on the Chinese side of the border, also survived, and the couple now stays in touch through video calls.

___

Associated Press journalists Rod McGuirk in Melbourne and Huizhong Wu in Bangkok contributed to this report.

अल्बानी न॑ आरू कहलकै, “हमरा सब क॑ आशा छै, निश्चित रूप स॑, आरू सकारात्मक खबर के, आरू हम्मं॑ अधिकारियऽ के साथ काम करै लेली हर संभव प्रयास करी रहलऽ छियै ।

नेपाल पर्यटन बोर्डक प्रवक्ता सुनील शर्मा कहलनि जे, पहिने लापता हेबाक सूचना भेटल कम सँ कम पाँचटा अन्य विदेशी पर्यटक हालक दिन मे ईमेल वा टेलीफोन माध्यम सँ अधिकारि सँ संपर्क केने छथि ।

चीन बचाव दल के लेल पहुंच सड़क बनबैत अछि

चीन दिस स बचाव दल नेपाल सीमा पर ग्यारोंग बंदरगाह पर आपदा स्थल तक पहुंचय वाला अस्थायी सड़क पूरा केलक, राज्य प्रसारक सीसीटीवी बुधदिन जानकारी देलक अछि।

बाढ़ि सं बहल सीमा पार परिसर मे खोज मे इस्तेमाल होबय वाला भारी मशीनरी के लेल चालक दल पहुंच साफ क रहल अछि. क्रासिंग दिस जायबला सड़क नष्ट भ गेल आ पानि, थाल आ पाथरक नीचा गाड़ि देल गेल।

चीन मे अलग-अलग रविदिन तक 16 लोक के मौत आओर 546 लोक के लापता होय के खबर अछि.

ई आपदा 26 अगस्त स॑ हिमालय म॑ शुरू होलै, जब॑ हिमनदी केरऽ पतन स॑ चट्टान, बर्फ आरू पिघललऽ पानी नीचें घाटी म॑ भेजलऽ गेलै, जेकरा स॑ नीचें म॑ शक्तिशाली बाढ़ आबी गेलै । ई लहर तिब्बत आ नेपाल स बहैत नदी मे प्रवेश केलक, जाहि स ओ नदी तेजी स बढ़ल। बाढ़िक पानि घर, भवन, सड़क आ पुल कए बहरा गेल, जाहि स थाल आ चट्टान कए नीचा ल गेल।

किछु बचि गेल लोक के काठमांडू मे आश्रय भेटैत छनि

बाढ़ि सँ बचि गेल किछु गोटे नेपालक राजधानी काठमांडू मे शरण लेबाक लेल तबाही सँ भागि रहल छथि ।

काठमांडू स॑ लगभग ११० किलोमीटर (६५ मील) पश्चिम दूर तिमुरे शहर केरऽ अधिकांश ४०० बची गेलऽ लोगऽ न॑ पीला गुम्बा मठ म॑ ठहरलऽ छै, साथ ही साथ परिवार केरऽ सदस्य आरू घरऽ के नुकसान के शोक मनाबै के साथ-साथ एक-दूसरा प॑ भरोसा करी रहलऽ छै । आश्रय स्थल केरऽ आयोजन स्थानीय आरू रिश्तेदारऽ द्वारा करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ व्यक्ति आरू चैरिटी संगठनऽ स॑ राहत केरऽ सामान आबी रहलऽ छै ।

मठ मे रहनिहार मे 21 वर्षीय रिया तामांग सेहो छथि, जे बाढ़िक पानि लग आबि गेला पर अपन 10 महीना क बच्चा क संग भागि गेलीह।

ओ कहलीह जे घर स बाहर निकलल हम अंतिम व्यक्ति छलहुं, भागब एतेक कठिन छल।

तमांग एहि आपदा मे अपन दादा-दादी केँ गमा लेलक। सीमा के चीनी तरफ ग्यरोंग शहर में रसोइया के काज करय वाला हुनकर पति सेहो बचि गेलाह आ आब ई जोड़ी वीडियो कॉल के माध्यम सं संपर्क में रहैत अछि.

___ २.

मेलबर्न केरऽ एसोसिएटेड प्रेस केरऽ पत्रकार रोड मैकगुइर्क आरू बैंकॉक केरऽ हुइझोंग वू न॑ ई रिपोर्ट म॑ योगदान देल॑ छै ।

full_article:
The road leading to the Gyirong border crossing between China and Nepal has been fully restored, just a week after it was destroyed in catastrophic flash floods.

The border crossing was torn apart when a glacier collapsed above the Nepal-Tibet border last week, sending a surge of ice, rock and mud through the valley below.

It is the main trade and transport link between China and Nepal in this part of the Himalayas, used for carrying goods and travellers over the mountains to the Nepali border town of Rasuwagadhi. Its destruction had left rescue teams struggling to reach some of the worst-affected areas on the Chinese side.

It comes as Nepalese rescuers pulled 118 more people to safety with the help of helicopters and other air assets.

He was distributing aid to communities cut off by collapsed bridges, and was mistaken for a flood survivor when he returned to Kathmandu on a humanitarian aid helicopter and gave his details to a police officer at the army barracks.

नेपाल पर्यटन बोर्ड के प्रवक्ता सुनील शर्मा के कहनाय छनि जे पहिने सं लापता भेल कम सं कम पांचटा आओर विदेशी पर्यटक फोन या ईमेल सं अधिकारी सं संपर्क केने छथिन्ह.

चीन केरऽ विदेश मंत्रालय न॑ कहलकै कि हुनी डीएनए जांच विशेषज्ञ आरू राहत केरऽ एगो आरू बैच भेजतै, जेकरा म॑ ड्रोन आरू जल शुद्धिकरण उपकरण भी शामिल छै । श्री शाह कहलनि जे, आपदा के बाद नेपाल मे 42 मिलियन डॉलर सं बेसी के सहायता के प्रवाह भेल अछि, जाहि मे आओर योगदान के उम्मीद अछि.

In the aftermath of the floods, families need safe drinking water, hygiene supplies, healthcare, nutritious food and shelter. Clean water and hygiene kits help prevent the spread of disease, while health care and nutrition support can save lives and help children stay healthy. Many families have lost access to these essentials after roads, water systems, and other infrastructure were damaged.

Malnutrition is also a major concern. Floods can disrupt food supplies, healthcare services and family incomes, making it harder for children to get the nutrition they need. Children who are already vulnerable are at greater risk of becoming malnourished, and those with severe acute malnutrition require specialised treatment to survive and recover. UNICEF is working to deliver therapeutic food to affected communities, but growing needs are placing additional pressure on available supplies.

Children also need protection, emotional support and access to education. Around 10,000 school-aged children now require urgent assistance to continue learning, including temporary learning spaces and replacement of school supplies.
translated:
बाढ़ि के बाद परिवार के सुरक्षित पेयजल, स्वच्छता के सामान, स्वास्थ्य सेवा, पौष्टिक भोजन आ आवास के जरूरत छै. स्वच्छ पानी आ स्वच्छता किट बीमारी कें प्रसार कें रोकएय मे मदद करएयत छै, जखन कि स्वास्थ्य देखभाल आ पोषण कें सहायता जान बचा सकएय छै आ बच्चाक कें स्वस्थ रहएय मे मदद कयर सकएय छै. सड़क, जल प्रणाली, आ अन्य बुनियादी ढाँचा कें नुकसान पहुंचला कें बाद बहुत परिवारक कें इ आवश्यक वस्तुअक कें पहुंच खत्म भ गेल छै.

कुपोषण सेहो एकटा पैघ चिंता के विषय अछि। बाढ़ि खाद्य आपूर्ति, स्वास्थ्य देखभाल सेवाक आ परिवारक कें आय मे बाधा पहुंचा सकएय छै, जइ सं बच्चाक कें जरूरत कें पोषण भेटनाय मुश्किल भ सकएय छै. जे बच्चाक पइहले सं कमजोर छै, ओकरा कुपोषित हुअ कें बेसि खतरा होयत छै, आ जेकरा गंभीर तीव्र कुपोषण छै, ओकरा जीवित रहएय आ ठीक हुअ कें लेल विशेष उपचार कें आवश्यकता होयत छै. यूनिसेफ प्रभावित समुदायक कें चिकित्सीय भोजन पहुंचाबय कें काज कयर रहल छै, मुदा बढ़ैत जरूरतक कें कारण उपलब्ध आपूर्ति पर अतिरिक्त दबाव पड़ रहल छै.

बच्चाक कें सुरक्षा, भावनात्मक सहायता आ शिक्षा कें पहुंच कें सेहो जरूरत छै. आब स्कूली उम्र कें लगभग 10,000 बच्चाक कें सीखनाय जारी रखय कें लेल तत्काल सहायता कें आवश्यकता छै, जइ मे अस्थायी सीखय कें जगह आ स्कूली सामान बदलनाय शामिल छै.

description: Death toll from Nepal-China floods rises to 1,130, nearly 4,500 missing  TRT World
publisher.title: TRT World
full_article:
The death toll from last week’s flash floods and mudslides along the China-Nepal border has risen to 1,130, with nearly 4,500 people still missing, according to official data released on Wednesday.

Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said 1,114 bodies had been recovered since massive flash floods hit the Himalayan country on August 26. It said 292 people had been injured and 3,916 remained missing.

Authorities said about 12,000 people had been rescued from flood-hit areas, while more than 21,000 security personnel, including army and police, had been deployed to support search and rescue operations.

About 1.6 million people have been affected by the floods in Nepal, according to the authority.

title: Nepal floods: Father borrows $13, walks for days to search for missing son - Al Jazeera
description: Nepal floods: Father borrows $13, walks for days to search for missing son  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
Kathmandu/Nuwakot, Nepal — Talka Sada’s eyes are exhausted, the wrinkles on his face deep with worry. His heels hurt after walking long miles across Nepal’s mountains. He’s hungry and angry, but as his mood shifts between hope and helplessness, his focus remains on his mission: a desperate search for his son.

Sada, who is in his 50s, is from Saptari, a district in Nepal’s Terai region — the plains that stretch across southern Nepal, south of the Shivalik Hills and north of the porous border with India.

People from this part of the Himalayan nation are known as Madhesis, a distinct ethnolinguistic population with a diverse regional, cultural and caste identity. Vinod, his only son — Sada also has three daughters — has been missing since the devastating flash floods of August 26 destroyed homes, schools, bridges, power plants and everything in their path in large parts of northern Nepal.

Sada last spoke to 19-year-old Vinod a day before the floods that grew from the Bhotekoshi river. Vinod had come to the Rasuwa district, the region worst affected by the floods, a month earlier to work as a labourer at a hydropower plant. He would mix cement and take on other odd jobs. Four other young men who worked with him — all between 17 and 19 years old — are also missing since the floods.

“I can’t tell you how much my wife is howling. I am in deep pain myself and I do not know what to do,” Sada says as he wipes his tears.

Talka Sada, right, and his brother are searching for Sada’s son, who has been missing since the August 25 floods that devastated large parts of northern Nepal [Smita Sharma/ Al Jazeera]

Search, trek, search again

Dressed in a faded white shirt and black pants, the father wears an orange polythene bag as a raincoat. He carries a grey backpack on his shoulders. With him is his brother, Sada’s companion on a long and increasingly frustrating journey.

Advertisement

Sada shows a dirty handkerchief in his pocket with notes amounting to less than 2,000 Nepali rupees (about $13) crumpled in it. It’s money he borrowed to be able to crisscross Nepal’s flood-affected areas in search of his son.

“I borrowed money to come all the way from Saptari to here. I have to pay an interest of 20 rupees on every 100 rupees I have borrowed,” he says. The brothers used some of that money to take a bus from Saptari to the national capital, Kathmandu. That 292km (181-mile) journey takes nine hours because of Nepal’s hilly terrain.

In Kathmandu, Sada and his brother went from hospital to hospital to look for Vinod among survivors or in the list of those declared dead — many of the flood victims were flown into Kathmandu from the northern parts of Nepal.

Outside mortuaries, the photographs displayed are often difficult to recognise. Most bodies being retrieved are decomposed or dismembered. There was no sign of Vinod — nor his name or photo at the hospitals.

So, Sada started walking towards Nuwakot (nearly 60km away from Kathmandu), closer to the location of the hydropower plant where his son was believed to be working.

After a gruelling, hours-long walk through broken roads, they reached Trishuli, a town on the way whose market now lies covered with debris, mud and slush.

“Last night when we reached here, a lodge charged us 1,500 Nepali rupees to stay the night. They gave us only one small serving of rice that did not even satisfy our hunger,” says Sada. “Now if we have to stay here another night, all my remaining money will finish and I will be left with nothing to go back home.”

Nepal army soldiers work during a search and rescue operation outside a tunnel near a hydropower project site, following deadly flash floods and mudslides, in Rasuwa district, Nepal, on September 1, 2026 [Nepal army/ Reuters]

‘They are pushing us away’

Sada and his brother say they just want access to mortuaries and army camps set up to help evacuate survivors and take bodies from the disaster zone, but claim that he has been turned away repeatedly.

To the brothers, the response they’ve received to their pleas for help is a product of deep-seated ethnic and caste divisions within Nepal. Madhesis — as the people of the Terai are known — have long accused the hills-based Nepali elite of discriminating against them.

Sada’s family is from the Musahar community, a particularly marginalised community that lives in the Terai and in the Indian states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

“We are poor. They think of us as Madheshis and Biharis. We cannot speak Nepali fluently — which is why they are just pushing us away and making us run from pillar to post,” Sada claims, as he sobs. “Even if it is a corpse, we have a right to see it. We have registered our names everywhere – police stations to military camps. But no one is helping us.”

Advertisement

Nepali authorities, overwhelmed by the scale of the crisis — more than 1,000 people have been killed, and thousands are still missing — insist they are trying their best to reach and help all survivors.

Nepal’s army personnel carry the bodies of flood victims during a search operation along the Narayani river at Bharatpur in Nepal’s Chitwan district on August 31, 2026 [Prakash Mathema/ AFP]

Helplessness and anger

The brothers try dialling Vinod’s phone number for the umpteenth time, but get no response. “We can’t talk to him. We don’t hear his voice. So everyone is heartbroken back home,” says Sada. “My wife asked me to get our son back. So we are searching all hydropower plants, but where do I find him?”

One minute, Sada is hoping for a miracle. “My son is young. He is a porter. He is daily wager. So he is agile. He could have surely walked, ran somewhere,” he wonders.

The very next moment, though, the father’s voice rings with helplessness. “I have no hope,” he says. “If Vinod was alive, he surely would have called from somewhere, even if he went to drink water.”

Yet giving up isn’t an option — not yet, at least.

So, Sada and his brother prepare to continue their trek towards the power plant where Vinod worked. As they leave, the father issues a warning that rings with a sense of betrayal and anger.

“We will have to burn down the police station if no one answers or helps us,” he shouts.
translated:
काठमांडू/नुवाकोट, नेपाल — तालका सदाक आँखि थकित अछि, चेहरा पर झुर्री चिंता सँ गहींर अछि । नेपाल’क पहाड़ पार क’ लंबा मील पैदल चललाक बाद हुनकर एड़ी मे दर्द भ’ गेलैन्ह. भूखल आ तमसाएल अछि, मुदा जेना-जेना ओकर मनोदशा आशा आ लाचारी’क बीच बदलैत जाइत छैक, ओकर ध्यान ओकर मिशन पर रहैत छैक: बेटा’क हताश खोज.

सदा, जे 50 के दशक में छै, नेपाल के तराई क्षेत्र के एक जिला सप्तरी के छै — जे मैदान दक्षिणी नेपाल, शिवालिक पहाड़ी के दक्षिण आरू भारत के झरझरा सीमा के उत्तर में फैलल छै.

हिमालय राष्ट्रक एहि भागक लोक मधेशीक नाम सँ जानल जाइत अछि, जे विविध क्षेत्रीय, सांस्कृतिक आ जातिगत पहिचानक संग एकटा विशिष्ट नृभाषिक आबादी अछि | विनोद, हुनकऽ एकलौता बेटा — सदा केरऽ भी तीन बेटी छै — जब॑ स॑ २६ अगस्त केरऽ विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ न॑ उत्तरी नेपाल केरऽ बड़ऽ हिस्सा म॑ घर, स्कूल, पुल, बिजली संयंत्र आरू ओकरऽ रास्ता म॑ सब कुछ तबाह करी देल॑ छै, तब॑ स॑ लापता छै ।

भोटेकोशी नदी स बढ़ल बाढ़ स एक दिन पहिने सदा अंतिम बेर 19 वर्षीय विनोद स गप केलथि। विनोद एक मास पहिने बाढ़ि स सबस बेसी प्रभावित क्षेत्र रसुवा जिला मे जलविद्युत संयंत्र मे मजदूर क काज करबा लेल आयल छलाह। सीमेंट मिला क' आन-आन विचित्र काज क' लैत छल। हुनका संग काज करय वाला चारिटा आओर युवक - सभ 17 सं 19 साल के बीच के - सेहो बाढ़ि के बाद लापता छथिन्ह.

सदा नोर पोछैत कहैत छथि, “हमर पत्नी कतेक हुंकारि रहल छथि से नहि कहि सकैत छी, हम स्वयं गहींर पीड़ा मे छी आ हमरा नहि बुझल अछि जे की करी।”

तालका सदा, दाहिना, आ हुनकर भाई सदा के बेटा के खोज में लागल छथि, जे 25 अगस्त के उत्तरी नेपाल के पैघ हिस्सा के तबाह करय वाला बाढ़ के बाद सं लापता अछि [स्मिता शर्मा/ अल जजीरा].

खोज, ट्रेक, फेर खोज

फीका उज्जर कमीज आ कारी पैंट पहिरने पिता रेनकोट के रूप में नारंगी रंग के पॉलीथीन बैग पहिरने छथि । कान्ह पर धूसर रंगक बैग ल' क' चलैत छथि । हुनका संग हुनकर भाइ, सदा’क संगी छथि जे एकटा नमहर आ तेजी सँ निराशाजनक यात्रा पर छथि.

विज्ञापन

सदा जेबी मे एकटा गंदा गमछा देखाबैत छथि जाहि मे 2000 नेपाली रुपया (करीब 13 डॉलर) स कम के नोट झुरमुट क रहल अछि। ई त’ ओ पाइ छैक जे ओ उधार ल’ लेने छल जे नेपालक बाढ़ि प्रभावित इलाका मे अपन बेटाक खोज मे क्रॉस क’ सकैत छल.

ओ कहैत छथि जे सप्तरी स एतय तक पूरा रास्ता आबय लेल उधार लेलौं, हमरा हर 100 रुपया कर्ज पर 20 रुपया के ब्याज देबय पड़ैत अछि। ओहि पाइ मे सँ किछु भाइ लोकनि सप्तरी सँ राष्ट्रीय राजधानी काठमांडू बस मे बैसि गेलाह । नेपाल केरऽ पहाड़ी इलाका के कारण वू २९२ किमी (१८१ मील) के यात्रा म॑ नौ घंटा लगै छै ।

काठमांडू मे सदा आ हुनक भाइ अस्पताल सँ अस्पताल जाइत विनोद केँ बचि गेल लोकक बीच वा मृत घोषित लोकक सूची मे — बाढ़ि पीड़ित मे सँ बहुतो केँ नेपालक उत्तरी भाग सँ काठमांडू मे उड़ान भरि गेल छल |

मुर्दाघरऽ के बाहर प्रदर्शित फोटो क॑ अक्सर पहचानना मुश्किल होय जाय छै । बरामद कैल जा रहल अधिकांश लाश सड़ल या विच्छेदित भ जायत छै. विनोदक कोनो निशानी नहि छलैक — आ ने अस्पताल मे ओकर नाम वा फोटो ।

अस्तु, सदा नुवाकोट (काठमांडू सं लगभग 60 किलोमीटर दूर) दिस बढ़य लगलाह, जे जलविद्युत संयंत्रक स्थानक नजदीक अछि जतय हुनक बेटाक काज मानल जाइत छल.

टूटल-फूटल सड़क पर घंटों के थकाऊ, टहललाक बाद ओ लोकनि त्रिशुली पहुँचलाह, जे बाट पर एकटा एहन शहर अछि जकर बाजार आब मलबा, थाल-कादो आ कीचड़ सं आच्छादित पड़ल अछि.

सदा कहैत छथि, “काल्हि राति जखन हम सब एतय पहुंचलहुं त एकटा लॉज हमरा सब स 1500 नेपाली टका लेलक जे राति रुकबाक लेल, ओ सब हमरा सब कए मात्र एकटा छोट सन चाउर देलक जे भूख तक नहि पूरा केलक। “आब जँ एक राति आओर एत’ रह’ पड़त त’ हमर सभटा पाइ बचि जायत आ हमरा घर वापस जेबाक लेल किछु नहि रहि जायब।”

नेपाल के रसुवा जिला में 1 सितम्बर, 2026 को जलविद्युत परियोजना स्थल के समीप एक सुरंग के बाहर, घातक आकस्मिक बाढ़ एवं कीचड़ गिरला के बाद, नेपाल सेना के जवान कार्यरत [नेपाल सेना/ रायटर]

‘हमरा सभकेँ धकेलि रहल अछि’।

सदा आरू हुनकऽ भाई के कहना छै कि हुनी बस चाहै छै कि बची क॑ निकलै वाला लोगऽ क॑ बाहर निकालै आरू आपदा क्षेत्र स॑ लाश लेबै म॑ मदद लेली बनालऽ गेलऽ शवदाह गृह आरू सेना केरऽ कैंप तक पहुँच, लेकिन दावा छै कि ओकरा बार-बार घुमाय देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

भाइ सब लेल मदद के गुहार के प्रति जे प्रतिक्रिया भेटल अछि ओ नेपाल के भीतर गहींर जातीय आ जातिगत विभाजन के उपज अछि. मधेशी — जेकरा तराई के लोग जानल जाय छै — बहुत दिन स॑ पहाड़ी स्थित नेपाली अभिजात वर्ग प॑ भेदभाव करै के आरोप लगैल॑ छै ।

सदा केरऽ परिवार मुसाहर समुदाय केरऽ छै, जे एगो विशेष रूप स॑ हाशिया प॑ पड़लऽ समुदाय छै जे तराई आरू भारतीय राज्य उत्तर प्रदेश आरू बिहार म॑ रहै छै ।

“हमरा सब गरीब छी, ओ सब हमरा सब के मधेशी आ बिहारी बुझैत छथि। हम सब नेपाली धाराप्रवाह नहि बाजि सकैत छी — जाहि कारण स ओ सब हमरा सब के बस दूर धकेलि रहल छथि आ एकटा खंभा स दोसर पोस्ट पर दौड़ा रहल छथि।'' सदा सिसकैत दावा करैत छथि। ओ कहलनि जे, भले ओ लाश हो, हमरा सब के देखबाक अधिकार अछि, हम सब अपन नाम सब ठाम दर्ज केने छी – थाना स ल कए मिलिट्री कैंप तक। मुदा कियो हमरा सभक मददि नहि क’ रहल अछि।”

विज्ञापन

संकट केरऽ पैमाना स॑ अभिभूत नेपाली अधिकारी — १,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै, आरू हजारों लोग अखनी भी लापता छै — के कहना छै कि हुनी सब बची गेलऽ लोगऽ तलक पहुँचै आरू मदद करै के पूरा कोशिश करी रहलऽ छै ।

नेपाल के चितवन जिला के भरतपुर में 31 अगस्त 2026 को नारायणी नदी के किनारे तलाशी अभियान के दौरान बाढ़ पीड़ित के शव ल क नेपाल के सेना के जवान [प्रकाश मथेमा/ एएफपी]

लाचारी आ क्रोध

भाइ लोकनि अनगिनत बेर विनोद’क फोन नंबर डायल करबाक प्रयास करैत छथि, मुदा कोनो प्रतिक्रिया नहि भेटैत छनि. “हमरा सभ हुनका स’ गप्प नहि क’ सकैत छी। हम हुनकर आवाज नहि सुनैत छी। तेँ घर वापसी मे सबहक हृदय टूटि गेल अछि।'' सदा कहैत छथि, ''हमर पत्नी हमरा अपन बेटा केँ वापस करबाक लेल कहलनि। त हम सब जलविद्युत संयंत्र मे खोजि रहल छी, मुदा हमरा ओ कतय भेटत?”

एक मिनट सदा एकटा चमत्कार के आशा में अछि। “हमर बेटा छोट अछि। ओ पोर्टर छथि। ओ नित्य दांव लगाबैत छथि। तेँ ओ फुर्तीला छथि। ओ जरूर चल सकैत छल, कतहु दौड़ि सकैत छल।-ओ आश्चर्यचकित होइत अछि।

मुदा, ठीक अगिला क्षण पिता’क आवाज मे लाचारी बजैत छैक. ओ कहैत छथि, “हमरा कोनो आशा नहि अछि। “ विनोद जीबैत रहितथि तऽ कतहु सँ जरूर फोन करितथि, भले ओ पानि पीबय चलि गेल होथि।”

तइयो हार मानब कोनो विकल्प नहिं — एखन धरि नहि, कम स’ कम.

अस्तु, सदा आ ओकर भाइ अपन ट्रेक जारी रखबाक तैयारी करैत छथि जे ओहि पावर प्लांट दिस जतय विनोद काज केने छलाह. जाइत-जाइत पिता एकटा चेतावनी जारी करैत छथि जे विश्वासघात आ क्रोधक भाव सँ बजैत अछि ।

ओ चिचियाइत कहैत छथि जे, जौं कियो जवाब नहि देत आ ने मदद करत त थाना जरा देबय पड़त।

full_article:
Nepal is seeking "climate-related compensation" from the United States, India, and China -- which the Himalayan nation named as the major greenhouse emitters -- for deadly flash floods in the Bhotkoshi River that swept away villages across at least three districts in the country a week ago. So far, emergency teams have recovered more than 1,100 bodies, but nearly 4,500 people still remain missing after the gigantic wave of freezing water, rocks, and debris triggered by a high-altitude glacial collapse roared down the Tibet-Nepal border last week.

Launching a diplomatic pitch to seek international monetary assistance, Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal asserted that post-disaster aid should be treated as a matter of "moral liability," "not charity."

The minister said in Nepali during an interview with Kantipur TV, the excerpts of which were published by The Kathmandu Post newspaper and news agency PTI.

ALSO READ: Nepal's Floods, Bihar's Rivers: The Health Threat That Travels Downstream

Nepal Asks for Accountability

AFP

He pointed out that despite contributing "virtually negligible" greenhouse gas emissions, Nepal is bearing the disproportionate consequences of global warming, including rapid glacier melt and extreme mountain disasters.

"We are paying the ultimate price for a global crisis we did not create. The rapid melting of glaciers and these catastrophic mountain tsunamis are direct consequences of global climate change," he said, per excerpts of his interview published by PTI.

Khanal said Nepal is shifting its diplomatic framework from "aid" to "justice and compensation". "This is not a matter of charity; it is a matter of legal and moral liability."

"The major industrial emitters -- such as China, which is the world's top emitter, the United States at number two, and India at number three -- have a historical responsibility to compensate vulnerable nations like Nepal," he said.

ALSO READ: Non-Stop Choppers, 48-Hour Queues: Inside Nepal's Himalayan Rescue

The Culprits

Khanal said Kathmandu plans to raise the issue of climate change "with absolute firmness and clarity" at international forums. He said the country will also seek compensation from major emitters for climate-related losses suffered by vulnerable countries.

"This is a matter of civilisational survival. If our Himalayan glaciers disappear, the water security of over two billion people in South Asia dependent on rivers like the Ganges and the Trishuli will be permanently compromised. We are advocating not just for Nepal, but for the survival of South Asian civilization," he said.

The minister said Nepal's finance ministry has officially dispatched a formal climate compensation claim letter to its international partners.

"If our Himalayan glaciers disappear, the water security of over two billion people in South Asia -- dependent on rivers like the Ganges and the Trishuli -- will be permanently compromised. We are advocating not just for Nepal but for the survival of South Asian civilization," he added.

ALSO READ: "Bhaago, bhaago": Assam Man Was Stuck On Hill For 4 Days After Nepal Flood

India's Stand

AFP

India has repeatedly emphasised climate equity and highlighted its relatively low per capita emissions. New Delhi argues that climate obligations should take into account differences in countries' historical emissions, development needs, and capacities.

New Delhi has supported efforts to address loss and damage suffered by vulnerable developing countries and maintains that Western nations, which industrialised first, occupy the majority of the global carbon budget.

It also maintains that developed countries should provide the necessary financial resources to help such nations deal with climate impacts.

Nepal's Call for Aid

Nepal has formally approached the board of the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, seeking urgent financial assistance following the catastrophic flash flood in the Bhotekoshi river basin on August 26, according to The Kathmandu Post report.

The mechanism was established at COP27 in 2022 and operationalised at COP28.

A letter jointly signed by Nepal's Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Forests and Agriculture Minister Geeta Chaudhary has sought an urgent response to the catastrophic flash flood, which caused widespread loss of life, displacement, and destruction of homes and critical infrastructure.

"The full scale of economic and non-economic loss and damage has yet to be determined; however, preliminary information indicates that the consequences are extensive and exceed Nepal's immediate response capacity," the letter said.

title: Hopes of finding survivors dim a week after catastrophic Nepal flood - CBC
description: Hopes of finding survivors dim a week after catastrophic Nepal flood  CBC
publisher.title: CBC
full_article:
Hopes of finding more survivors among the thousands still missing in Nepal were fading, authorities said on Wednesday, a week after a glacier collapse in the Himalayas unleashed flash floods that devastated the mountainous nation.

At least 1,114 people have been killed and nearly 4,000 remain unaccounted for, with officials fearing many are buried under debris left by the floods that tore through towns and valleys near the Chinese border.

Across the border in Tibet, China's official toll has held steady since Sunday at 16 dead and 546 missing.

"The hope of finding survivors is decreasing," Phanindra Paudel, a senior official at the government’s National Emergency Operation Center (NEOC), said. "We pray and are hopeful. Hope is hope!"

More than 1,000 dead from catastrophic Nepal-China floods as rescuers search for survivors

Nepal flash flood death toll climbs to 579, with 32 Canadians, permanent residents among missing

Rescuers are trying to find survivors believed to be trapped inside the tunnels of several hydroelectric plants, whose powerhouses have spaces and rooms for people to stay, army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said.

Ayusha Timalsina, wife of Suraj Timalsina, who was killed in the deadly floods and a mudslide, mourns during his cremation rituals using an effigy (not pictured) as his body remained missing, in Kathmandu, Nepal. (Navesh Chitrakar/Reuters)

Authorities said 279 people had been rescued from the ruins of hydropower projects but at least 639 more were still missing, some of whom are believed to be trapped in tunnels.

Specialized rescue teams from India, China and the United States were involved in the tunnel rescue attempts, authorities said.

Tunnels search continues

"The plan today is to get on a helicopter and go to the hydro tunnels where they believe there's still life," Ferrin Cole, a member of the U.S. crisis response team that is currently in Nepal, told ANI news agency.

"We have high-technology listening equipment to listen for sounds of life. And then the safety teams to go in and check."

"Looking at the nature of the disaster and the area which has been hit by the flood, as days go by there are less chances of human survivors," Binoj Basnet, a retired senior army general who oversaw the search and rescue operation during the 2015 earthquake in which about 9,000 people were killed, said.

Rescue workers and officials manage a mass burial trench for unidentified remains recovered after severe flash floods in Nepal. (Amit Shukla/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty Images)

Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the focus would shift from search, rescue and relief operations towards rehabilitation and reconstruction.

"The government is now focusing on rehabilitation while working to protect the lives of people in the affected areas and providing necessary medical treatment and psychological counseling," Shah said in a late-night post on social media on Tuesday.

The disaster left at least 2.2 million tons of debris, according to a preliminary estimate by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), including parts of buildings, rocks, and sediment, the equivalent of six Empire State buildings.

Residents in affected areas walked around the remains of what were once bustling villages and towns, trying to salvage whatever they could of their belongings.

"My husband and I were able to escape safely. But we could not pick up anything," Shanta Sunar, 45, a small shopkeeper and survivor from Nuwakot, said.

"We have lost whatever we had. But we are lucky nothing happened to us."

Growing public health risk

United Nations spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said aid agencies were concerned about the growing public health risk from overcrowded shelters, contaminated water and damaged health facilities, particularly for women and children during the monsoon season.

About 3,900 people remain unaccounted for and nearly 3,500 people are living in 27 displacement sites across the hardest-hit districts of Nuwakot and Rasuwa, Dujarric told a regular UN press briefing on Tuesday.

Shah said his government had stepped up surveillance and response measures to prevent possible outbreaks of disease in flood-affected areas.

title: Nepal’s mountain tourism industry faces ‘serious warning’ after Himalayan flood disaster - CNBC
description: Nepal’s mountain tourism industry faces ‘serious warning’ after Himalayan flood disaster  CNBC
publisher.title: CNBC
full_article:
An aerial view shows houses lying deluged in sludge after flash floods at Devighat, Bidur Municipality in Nepal's Nuwakot district on August 27, 2026. Prabin Ranabhat | Afp | Getty Images

Nepal's renowned adventure tourism industry faces a sobering reality check, according to local mountain tourist associations and hostel owners, following devastating flooding on Nepal's border with China. The death toll from last week's disaster, which tore through villages along the Nepal-Tibet border, stood at 987, authorities said Tuesday. Nearly 4,250 people were missing, they added. The catastrophe began on Aug. 26 in the Himalayas, a mountain range that contains some of the world's highest peaks, including the highest, Mount Everest. A massive glacial collapse in northern Nepal triggered a landslide of ice and rock and meltwater into the valleys below, with powerful floods sweeping away or cutting off entire communities and damaging roads, bridges and hydropower facilities. The tragedy, which prompted Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah to push for international climate action, underscores the growing impact of climate change on adventure tourism. Rajendra Bahadur Lama, general secretary of the Nepal Mountaineering Association, described the floods as a "serious warning" for Nepal's tourism industry. "This disaster should not be seen as the end of Nepal's adventure tourism; it should be a wake-up call," Lama told CNBC in an email. "Climate change is changing the Himalayas, and Nepal must now build a tourism industry that is not only adventurous, but safer, smarter and climate-resilient."

Read more Nepal resumes flood rescue, seeks technical help and billions of dollars More storms possible at Grand Canyon where a flash flood killed 1 person and left 15 missing How a lesser-known climate phenomenon is threatening from above

Tourism infrastructure, routes and destinations will need to be assessed and redesigned with better protection for floods, landslides and other extreme events, Lama said, noting that international tourists are "increasingly conscious" of climate change and safety.

Counting the cost

To rebuild from the catastrophe, Nepal, one of the least developed countries in South Asia, has reportedly estimated a cost of between $4 billion and $5 billion, equivalent to nearly one-tenth of its economy. The tourism industry is a core tenet of the Nepalese economy and serves as a major source of foreign exchange and revenue. The country of nearly 30 million is world-renowned as a hotspot for trekking and mountaineering, as well as a premier global destination for spiritual travel. Tourists have cancelled bookings in the last several days, however, just as Nepal heads into its most popular travel season from Sept. 15 to Nov. 15, said Saroj Bhandari, owner of the Wander Thirst hostel in the capital city of Kathmandu, more than five hours' drive from the flood site.

The aerial view shows Swayambhunath Stupa in Kathmandu, Nepal, on October 21, 2025. Nurphoto | Nurphoto | Getty Images

Bhandari expects that, at best, his 122-bed hostel will reach 60% occupancy during that peak tourist season this year, down from 100% last year. Most of the cancellations have come from European tourists, he said. "This time only the one part of Nepal is little damaged by the flood and a lot of the tourists think it's not safe to go to Nepal because of that," he said, noting the country does not only consist of mountains but also flatland. Bhandari said Nepal is nearing the end of its rainy monsoon season. He emphasized the government's system for landslide alerts and road closures, noting the state typically shares warnings about floods and landslides with the hostel every day, which the hostel then passes on to guests. While he was not aware whether China had sent an alert, Bhandari said people who first saw the flood had warned those living downstream of it, but that those downstream had underestimated its size. A spokesperson for Nepal's government was not immediately available to respond when contacted by CNBC. China's Foreign Ministry, meanwhile, has said it is preparing a third batch of emergency aid for Nepal and will continue to "stand firmly together" with its neighboring country.

watch now VIDEO 2:56 02:56 Why there's no 'offseason' travel anymore Transportation

Tibet Vista, a regional tour organizer with offices in Nepal and China, meanwhile, said in a statement to CNBC that all its travelers and team members were safe. "None of our guests were at Gyirong Port when the flooding occurred, and no travelers with Tibet Vista were affected by the disaster," Tibet Vista said Monday. "We are deeply saddened by what happened, and our thoughts are with the victims, their families, and everyone affected by this tragedy."

Severe glacial flood risks

The U.S. embassy in China on Aug. 30 noted the risk of further landslides and flooding due to additional rainfall through Sept. 1. Beijing had sent Premier Li Qiang to visit the flood site on Aug. 27 and focused a regular month-end meeting of top leaders on response to the catastrophe, with a readout noting the disaster occurred in a cold plateau region surrounded by glaciers and potential hazards. An assistant secretary-general at the United Nations on Tuesday warned that millions of people in the Himalayan region were at risk from glacial floods, with fears that entire riverbanks might become effectively uninhabitable. "Technology cannot move fast enough to prevent loss along these massive river systems that catch the overflow of the glacier lakes," Kanni Wignaraja, an assistant secretary-general at the U.N., told Reuters in an interview. Researchers have previously identified 47 dangerous glacial lakes in Nepal, China and India, although the real number has since been estimated to be far higher.

This photograph taken on May 20, 2026, shows mountaineers climbing a slope lined up during their ascent from the Hillary Step to summit Mount Everest in Nepal. Furte Sherpa | Afp | Getty Images

"The devastating impacts of the Nepal floods cannot be understated," Carlo Buontempo, director of the European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service (CS3), told CNBC by email. "While the precise chain of events that led to this disaster will take time to reconstruct, the wider picture is already clear: the world's frozen regions are losing mass, and as they do, they are becoming less stable." Indeed, as the climate warms, Buontempo said the loss of glacial ice around the world would have important consequences for mountainous landscapes. "Glaciers buttress the slopes around them; frozen ground holds fractured rock in place; meltwater collects in lakes behind fragile natural dams. As the ice thins and the permafrost thaws, mountains that were held together for millennia begin to loosen their grip," he added.

This photograph shows the small village of Blatten, in the Bietschhorn mountain of the Swiss Alps, destroyed by a landslide after part of the huge Birch Glacier collapsed and swallowed up by the river Lonza the day before, in Blatten on May 29, 2025. Alexandre Agrusti | Afp | Getty Images

This process typically happens slowly, but sometimes it can happen suddenly — such as when a massive ice and rock collapse onto Switzerland's Birch Glacier buried the Alpine village of Blatten in May last year. "The Nepal floods underscore the importance of continued satellite monitoring for early-warning signs, to inform future risk planning and be able to save villages, as in the case of Blatten where residents were evacuated before the landslide. It is evident that the climate of the past has shifted – we must redouble our efforts in preparing for the future," Buontempo said.

नेपाल केरऽ प्रसिद्ध साहसिक पर्यटन उद्योग क॑ चीन के साथ नेपाल केरऽ सीमा प॑ विनाशकारी बाढ़ के बाद स्थानीय पहाड़ी पर्यटक संघ आरू छात्रावास मालिकऽ के अनुसार गंभीर वास्तविकता जांच के सामना करना पड़॑ छै । नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमाक गाम-गाम फाड़ि गेल पिछला सप्ताहक आपदा सँ मृतकक संख्या ९८७ रहल अधिकारी मंगलदिन जनौलक अछि । ओ सब इहो कहलनि जे, करीब 4250 लोक लापता अछि। ई प्रलय 26 अगस्त क॑ हिमालय म॑ शुरू होय गेलऽ छेलै, जे एगो पर्वत श्रृंखला छेकै जेकरा म॑ दुनिया केरऽ कुछ सबसें ऊंचऽ चोटी छै, जेकरा म॑ सबस॑ ऊँचऽ माउंट एवरेस्ट भी शामिल छै । उत्तरी नेपाल केरऽ भारी हिमनदी केरऽ पतन के वजह स॑ नीचें के घाटी म॑ बर्फ आरू चट्टान आरू पिघललऽ पानी के भूस्खलन शुरू होय गेलै, जेकरा म॑ शक्तिशाली बाढ़ न॑ पूरा समुदाय क॑ बहाय देलकै या कटैलकै आरू सड़क, पुल आरू जलविद्युत सुविधा क॑ नुकसान पहुँचैलकै । नेपाली प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन्द्र शाह अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय जलवायु कार्यवाहीके लेल धकेलबला ई त्रासदी साहसिक पर्यटनमे जलवायु परिवर्तनके बढैत प्रभावके रेखांकित करैत अछि । नेपाल पर्वतारोहण संघके महासचिव राजेन्द्र बहादुर लामा बाढिके नेपालके पर्यटन उद्योगके लेल “गंभीर चेतावनी” बतौलनि । लामा सीएनबीसी कए ईमेल मे कहला जे एहि आपदा कए नेपाल क साहसिक पर्यटन क अंत नहि मानल जेबाक चाही, इ एकटा जागरण हेबाक चाही। "जलवायु परिवर्तन हिमालय क॑ बदली रहलऽ छै, आरू नेपाल क॑ अब॑ एगो ऐन्हऽ पर्यटन उद्योग के निर्माण करना छै जे न सिर्फ साहसिक होय, बल्कि सुरक्षित, होशियार आरू जलवायु के प्रति लचीला होय।"

बाढ़, भूस्खलन आरू अन्य चरम घटना स॑ बेहतर सुरक्षा के साथ पर्यटन बुनियादी ढाँचा, मार्ग आरू गंतव्यऽ के आकलन आरू नया रूप दै के जरूरत होतै, लामा न॑ कहलकै कि अंतरराष्ट्रीय पर्यटक जलवायु परिवर्तन आरू सुरक्षा के प्रति ‘बढ़ी स॑ जागरूक’ छै ।

लागत के गिनती करैत

प्रलय स॑ पुनर्निर्माण लेली दक्षिण एशिया केरऽ सबसें कम विकसित देशऽ म॑ स॑ एक नेपाल न॑ ४ स॑ ५ अरब डॉलर के बीच के लागत के अनुमान लगैल॑ छै, जे ओकरऽ अर्थव्यवस्था के लगभग दसवां हिस्सा के बराबर छै । पर्यटन उद्योग नेपाली अर्थव्यवस्थाक एकटा मूल सिद्धांत अछि आ विदेशी मुद्रा आ राजस्वक प्रमुख स्रोतक काज करैत अछि । लगभग तीन करोड़ लोगऽ के ई देश ट्रेकिंग आरू पर्वतारोहण केरऽ हॉटस्पॉट के रूप म॑ विश्व प्रसिद्ध छै, साथ ही आध्यात्मिक यात्रा लेली एगो प्रमुख वैश्विक गंतव्य भी छै । पिछला कई दिन स पर्यटक बुकिंग रद्द क देलक अछि, हालांकि ठीक ओहिना जखन नेपाल 15 सितम्बर स 15 नवंबर तक अपन सबस लोकप्रिय यात्रा सीजन मे आबि रहल अछि, बाढ़ि स्थल स पांच घंटा स बेसी क ड्राइव पर राजधानी काठमांडू क वांडर थर्स्ट छात्रावास क मालिक सरोज भंडारी कहला।

हवाई दृश्य मे नेपाल के काठमांडू मे स्वयंभूनाथ स्तूप 21 अक्टूबर 2025 के देखाओल गेल अछि.Nurphoto | नुरफोटो | गेटी इमेजेज

भंडारी क॑ उम्मीद छै कि, बेहतरीन स्थिति म॑ हुनकऽ 122 बेड वाला हॉस्टल म॑ ई साल पर्यटन केरऽ वू चरम मौसम म॑ 60% कब्जा होय जैतै, जे पिछला साल 100% स॑ कम छै । ओ कहला जे अधिकांश रद्द यूरोपीय पर्यटक स आयल अछि। ओ कहलनि जे, एहि बेर नेपाल के एकटा हिस्सा मात्र बाढ़ि सं कम नुकसान पहुंचल अछि आ बहुत रास पर्यटक के लगैत छनि जे एहि कारणे नेपाल जेनाइ सुरक्षित नहि अछि। भण्डारी कहलनि जे, नेपाल वर्षा मानसून के मौसम समाप्त होबय के करीब अछि। हुनी भूस्खलन के अलर्ट आरू सड़क बंद करै के सरकार केरौ व्यवस्था प जोर देलकै, ई नोट करतें हुअय राज्य आम तौर प हर रोज बाढ़ आरू भूस्खलन के बारे मँ चेतावनी हॉस्टल के साथ साझा करै छै, जेकरा बाद हॉस्टल मेहमानौ क पास करै छै । हुनका ई बात के जानकारी नै छेलै कि चीन न॑ अलर्ट भेजलकै कि नै, लेकिन भंडारी न॑ कहलकै कि जे लोगऽ न॑ पहलऽ बार बाढ़ क॑ देखलकै, वू लोगऽ न॑ एकरऽ नीचें रहै वाला लोगऽ क॑ चेतावनी देल॑ छै, लेकिन नीचें के लोग न॑ एकरऽ आकार क॑ कम आंकी लेल॑ छै । सीएनबीसी सं संपर्क केला पर नेपाल सरकार के प्रवक्ता तत्काल कोनो जवाब देबय लेल उपलब्ध नहि छल. ओतहि चीनक विदेश मंत्रालय नेपाल लेल आपातकालीन सहायताक तेसर बैच तैयार क’ रहल अछि आ अपन पड़ोसी देशक संग ‘दृढ़तापूर्वक एक संग ठाढ़’ रहत।

ओतहि नेपाल आ चीन मे कार्यालय रखनिहार क्षेत्रीय भ्रमण आयोजक तिब्बत विस्टा सीएनबीसी केँ देल गेल बयान मे कहलनि जे, ओकर सभ यात्री आ टीमक सदस्य सुरक्षित छथि। तिब्बत विस्टा न॑ सोमवार क॑ कहलकै कि जब॑ बाढ़ आबी गेलऽ छेलै त॑ हमरऽ कोय भी मेहमान ग्यिरॉंग बंदरगाह प॑ नै छेलै, आरू तिब्बत विस्टा वाला कोय भी यात्री ई आपदा स॑ प्रभावित नै छेलै । "हमरा सब क॑ जे कुछ घटलै ओकरा स॑ बहुत दुख छै, आरू हमरऽ विचार पीड़ित, ओकरऽ परिवार, आरू ई त्रासदी स॑ प्रभावित सब के साथ छै ।"

गंभीर हिमनदी बाढ़ के जोखिम

चीन मे अमेरिकी दूतावास 1 अगस्त कए। 30 न॑ 1 सितंबर के माध्यम स॑ अतिरिक्त बारिश के कारण आरू भूस्खलन आरू बाढ़ के खतरा के नोट करलकै ।बीजिंग न॑ 27 अगस्त क॑ प्रीमियर ली कियांग क॑ बाढ़ स्थल के दौरा करै लेली भेजलकै आरू शीर्ष नेता सिनी के नियमित रूप स॑ महीना के अंत म॑ आयोजित बैठक क॑ प्रलय के प्रतिक्रिया प॑ केंद्रित करलकै, जेकरा म॑ एक रीडआउट म॑ नोट करलऽ गेलै कि ई आपदा ग्लेशियर आरू संभावित खतरा स॑ घिरलऽ ठंडा पठार क्षेत्र म॑ घटित होय गेलऽ छै । संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ एगो सहायक महासचिव न॑ मंगलवार क॑ चेतावनी देल॑ छै कि हिमालयी क्षेत्र केरऽ लाखों लोगऽ क॑ हिमनदीय बाढ़ के खतरा छै, जेकरा स॑ ई आशंका छै कि पूरा नदी के किनारे प्रभावी ढंग स॑ रह॑ सकै वाला नै होय सकै छै । यू.एन.के सहायक महासचिव कन्नी विगनाराज न॑ रायटर क॑ देलऽ गेलऽ साक्षात्कार म॑ कहलकै कि तकनीक एतना तेजी स॑ नै बढ़ी सकै छै कि ग्लेशियर झीलऽ के ओवरफ्लो क॑ पकड़ै वाला ई विशाल नदी प्रणाली के साथ नुकसान नै होय सक॑ । शोधकर्ता न॑ पहल॑ भी नेपाल, चीन आरू भारत केरऽ ४७ खतरनाक हिमनदी झील के पहचान करी चुकलऽ छै, हालांकि ओकरा बाद स॑ एकरऽ वास्तविक संख्या कहीं अधिक होय के अनुमान लगैलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

२० मई २०२६ क॑ लेलऽ गेलऽ ई फोटो म॑ पर्वतारोही न॑ हिलेरी स्टेप स॑ नेपाल केरऽ माउंट एवरेस्ट केरऽ शिखर प॑ चढ़ै के दौरान लाइन म॑ लगलऽ ढलान प॑ चढ़ी रहलऽ छै । फुर्ते शेर्पा | Afp | गेटी इमेजेज

यूरोपीय संघ केरऽ कोपर्निकस जलवायु परिवर्तन सेवा (सीएस३) केरऽ निदेशक कार्लो बुओन्टेम्पो न॑ ईमेल द्वारा सीएनबीसी क॑ बतैलकै कि नेपाल केरऽ बाढ़ केरऽ विनाशकारी प्रभाव क॑ कम नै कहलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै । "जखन कि ई आपदा केरऽ कारण बनलऽ घटना के सटीक श्रृंखला के पुनर्निर्माण म॑ समय लगतै, लेकिन एकरऽ व्यापक तस्वीर पहिने स॑ ही साफ छै: दुनिया केरऽ जमलऽ क्षेत्रऽ के द्रव्यमान घटत॑ जाय रहलऽ छै, आरू जेना-जेना ई आपदा होय रहलऽ छै, वू कम स्थिर होय रहलऽ छै ।" सचमुच, जलवायु गर्म होय के साथ-साथ बुओन्टेम्पो न॑ कहलकै कि दुनिया भर म॑ हिमनदी बर्फ केरऽ नुकसान स॑ पहाड़ी परिदृश्य लेली महत्वपूर्ण परिणाम होतै । हुनी आरू कहलकै, "ग्लेशियर ओकरऽ चारो तरफ के ढलान क॑ बट्रेस करै छै; जमलऽ जमीन टूटलऽ चट्टान क॑ जगह प॑ रखै छै; नाजुक प्राकृतिक बांधऽ के पीछू झीलऽ म॑ पिघललऽ पानी जमा होय जाय छै । जेना-जेना बर्फ पतला होय जाय छै आरू परमाफ्रॉस्ट पिघलऽ जाय छै, सहस्राब्दी स॑ एक साथ रखलऽ गेलऽ पहाड़ऽ के पकड़ ढीला होय जाय छै ।"

ई फोटो म॑ स्विस आल्प्स केरऽ बिएत्शॉर्न पहाड़ म॑ स्थित छोटऽ गाँव ब्लैटन क॑ दिखालऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरा एक दिन पहलें विशाल बर्च ग्लेशियर केरऽ कुछ हिस्सा गिरी क॑ लोन्जा नदी न॑ निगलला के बाद भूस्खलन स॑ तबाह होय गेलऽ छै, ब्लैटन म॑ २९ मई २०२५ क॑.. अलेक्जेंडर अग्रुस्टी | Afp | गेटी इमेजेज

ई प्रक्रिया आम तौर पर धीरे-धीरे होय छै, लेकिन कखनी-कखनी ई अचानक भी होय सकै छै — जेना कि जब॑ पिछला साल मई म॑ स्विट्जरलैंड केरऽ बर्च ग्लेशियर प॑ भारी बर्फ आरू चट्टान गिरी क॑ अल्पाइन गाँव ब्लैटन क॑ दफना देलकै । बुओन्टेम्पो कहलनि जे, नेपाल के बाढ़ि पूर्व चेतावनी संकेत के लेल उपग्रह निगरानी जारी रखबाक महत्व के रेखांकित करैत अछि, भविष्य के जोखिम योजना के जानकारी देबय लेल आ गाम के बचाबय में सक्षम हेबाक लेल, जेना ब्लाटन के मामला में जतय भूस्खलन सं पहिने निवासी के बाहर निकालल गेल छल. ई स्पष्ट अछि जे अतीत के जलवायु बदलि गेल अछि – भविष्य के तैयारी में हमरा सब के अपन प्रयास दुगुना करय पड़त।

गूगल पर सीएनबीसी के अपन पसंदीदा स्रोत के रूप मे चुनू आओर बिजनेस न्यूज मे सभ सं भरोसेमंद नाम सं एक पल सेहो नहिं छोड़ू.

description: UK aid worker says he was mistaken for survivor in Nepal  Yahoo
publisher.title: Yahoo
full_article:
A British aid worker has spoken about being mistaken as a survivor of Nepal's flash floods, after it was incorrectly announced he had been rescued.

Alastair Chambers, from Gloucester, said the mix-up happened when he returned to Kathmandu after flying back in a humanitarian aid helicopter from a village near the Trishuli river.

The 45-year-old told the Press Association: "I got dropped off at the army barracks, and when I got dropped off one of the police officers came up to me and asked for my details. Then they presumed that I'd been rescued. It's been a bit of a weird one, really."

"News spreads - I was contacted by about 15 different journalists in the last few hours, just asking how I was and how I'm feeling after being rescued, and I had to say: 'Well sorry, I haven't been rescued.'"

Chambers flew to Nepal last week after seeing the disaster that hit both Nepal and neighbouring Tibet, killing more than 1,000 people, with 3,900 still missing.

On Tuesday, Under-Secretary of State at the Foreign Office Lord Wood of Anfield told the House of Lords 36 British people were unaccounted for, up from the previous total of 33.

The Foreign Office has been contacted for comment.

Chambers said he worked with volunteers to distribute sleeping bags, water purification tools, food and essentials to communities cut off by collapsed bridges, travelling to the area by helicopter.

"It's quite dangerous, and we've got a lot of landslides, trees across the roads in front of us," he said.

The volunteer worker added the journey usually takes one and a half hours from Kathmandu but the flood damage meant it took eight or nine hours to arrive.

"Thankfully, it wasn't large as the other torrent of water, so we waited until that settled and then made our way down and helped locate bodies and deliver humanitarian aid for the last few days," he said.

"It's been quite challenging, but it's been very rewarding as well."

A former local councillor, he said he now intended to fly back to the UK to raise money for the devastated village before returning with essentials and set up solar powered lighting.

full_article:
"The moment the devastating flood came rushing into Nepal. This footage shows the terrifying force of the flash flood that struck Nepal on 26 August 2026," reads an Instagram post shared on August 29, 2026.

Text superimposed on the clip claims it shows the "first video of the flood coming in Nepal".

The video, which garnered more than 333,000 views, shows an avalanche hurtling down a mountainside towards a lake as two people can be seen moving away in the foreground.

Image Screenshot of the false Instagram post taken on September 1, with a red X added by AFP

The video, which was filmed weeks before the disaster, also circulated on Facebook and X with similar claims linking it to the floods in Nepal.

Devastating floods in the China-Nepal border killed at least 1,114 people in Nepal, while 3,916 remained missing, the disaster authority said on September 2 (archived links here and here).

Rescue teams are meanwhile digging, drilling and blasting through debris in an effort to reach around 100 hydropower workers believed trapped in multiple tunnels.

The US Geological Survey (USGS) says the disaster that struck the China-Nepal border on August 26 was triggered by a glacial collapse.

However this clip is unrelated to the disaster in Nepal.

Footage from Peru

A reverse image search on Google using keyframes from the false post found an identical Instagram video published on July 27 (archived link).

The Instagram video was captioned with the hashtags "avalanche, mountain, perù, humantay and lagoon".

Image Screenshot comparison of the false post clip (L) and the July Instagram video

The same user also posted another photo of himself sitting beside the same lake on July 28 (archived link).

A subsequent keyword search on Google found local media reports about an avalanche in Peru on July 27.

Local media reports said the Instagram video was filmed at Humantay Lagoon on July 27, 2026, when a large mass of ice broke off the snow-covered mountains above the glacial lake in Peru's Cusco region (archived links here, here).

No injuries or damage were reported, but local authorities had to reassess conditions at the popular tourist site following the avalanche.

The footage corresponds to geo-tagged images of the Humantay Lagoon uploaded on Google Maps (archived link).

Image Screenshot comparison of the false post (L) and a Google Maps photo

AFP has debunked other false claims swirling around the disaster in Nepal and Tibet.
